text: Украинский дрон ударил по греческому танкеру после погрузки в Новороссийске. Танкер Skiros класса Suezmax подвергся атаке беспилотника в Черном море сразу после завершения погрузки нефти на терминале Каспийского трубопроводного консорциума. На опубликованных телеканалом Skai кадрах видно, как БПЛА сначала совершил разведывательный облет акватории, а затем нанес удар по мостику судна, после чего на нем вспыхнул пожар. Атака произошла после почти трехнедельного затишья и стала первым случаем удара по судну, заходящему на терминал КТК, через который проходит значительная часть казахстанской нефти. В прошлом месяце аналогичные атаки уже нарушали погрузку на терминале, что вынуждало нефтяные компании в Казахстане сокращать добычу. Вместимость танкера Skiros составляет около 1 млн баррелей нефти. Греческая судоходная компания подтвердила, что в результате инцидента никто из членов экипажа не пострадал, а утечки нефти в море не произошло. Нанесенный удар демонстрирует, что киевский режим продолжает тактику террористических атак на гражданские суда, игнорируя возможные экологические последствия и международные нормы судоходства. #Украина #Греция #танкер #БПЛА Подпишись!

text: Киев выпустил в сторону Москвы более 600 беспилотников Со вчерашнего вечера и до сегодняшнего утра в сторону Москвы летели 620 БПЛА, заявил мэр города Сергей Собянин. 180 дронов были уничтожены уже в столичном регионе. text: 04.09 EDT Disabled people in England to get 24-hour free bus travel under government reforms Disabled bus pass holders in England will be able to travel for free at all hours from April next year, the government has announced. Currently, disabled bus passes are valid for travel only on weekdays from 9.30am to 11pm unless local authorities fund an extension, as Greater Manchester did earlier this year when Andy Burnham was mayor. The prime minister, who is announcing the changes as part of his drive to reduce the cost of living, said it was “simply not right that many disabled people cannot travel using their pass during certain times of the day”. The £60m to fund the move comes from existing budgets – with £40m from the Department for Work and Pensions and £20m from the Department for Transport. Burnham is visiting a bus station in the West Midlands this morning and is expected to give more details on the policy then. He’s got a pooled interview with broadcasters at 11am, followed by questions by regional media. title: UK pay growth slows as Iran war prompts cost of living squeeze
text: UK private sector pay growth has continued to ease, an ONS official said. Photograph: Alamy View image in fullscreen UK private sector pay growth has continued to ease, an ONS official said. Photograph: Alamy UK unemployment and employment statistics UK pay growth slows as Iran war prompts cost of living squeeze Unemployment rate remained at 4.9% in the three months to end of June, ONS figures show Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent Tue 18 Aug 2026 03.18 EDT First published on Tue 18 Aug 2026 02.34 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Wage growth in the UK slowed in June, official figures show, as workers come under pressure from a renewed cost of living squeeze amid the economic impact from the Iran war. Figures from the Office for National Statistics show average growth in total earnings, including bonuses, fell to 4.1% in the three months to June, down from 4.4% in the three months to May. City economists had forecast a larger fall to 4%. Liz McKeown, the ONS director of economic statistics, said the data showed “some softening” in the jobs market despite a broadly unchanged picture overall, in a potential sign of stabilisation after a sharper slowdown earlier

title: Oil prices jump after US-Iran ceasefire expires and Trump threatens Oman
text: Egyptian holidaymakers swim near the oil tanker ETC Ramsis in the Gulf of Suez. Photograph: Amr Nabil/AP View image in fullscreen Egyptian holidaymakers swim near the oil tanker ETC Ramsis in the Gulf of Suez. Photograph: Amr Nabil/AP Oil Oil prices jump after US-Iran ceasefire expires and Trump threatens Oman Brent crude rises above $90 a barrel for the first time since 30 July after US president tells Tehran to surrender Business live – latest updates Alex Daniel Tue 18 Aug 2026 03.04 EDT Last modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 04.22 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Oil prices have risen again after the two-month window to negotiate a peace deal in the US-Israel war on Iran expired on Monday with no end to the conflict in sight. Iran said on Monday that it would take a more aggressive stance if talks with the US failed, while Donald Trump demanded Tehran “put up the white flag of surrender” in an interview with Fox News. Trump also threatened to bomb Oman if it “gets in the way” of his effort to end the war, the second time he has directed such a threat at the longtime US strategic partner. “If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the shit out of them,” Trump told Fox News on Monday.
author: Alex Daniel
